facts.raw_span: A 36‐year‐old man of Indian origin presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute right‐sided weakness and three episodes of vomiting
He awoke around midnight with headache and vomiting, then noted right‐sided numbness and weakness
no visual change or speech disturbance
pulse was 88 bpm
blood pressure 124/87 mmHg
oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Motor strength was 0/5 in the right upper limb, 3/5 proximally and 2/5 distally in the right lower limb
Reflexes were brisk bilaterally with right ankle clonus
Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology
incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla
A diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a 36‐year‐old gentleman with no apparent risk factors was made

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and numbness, and brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla.
Noncontrast CT of the head showed an incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma.
The patient was diagnosed with ischemic stroke, but no apparent risk factors were identified.
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla.
The patient had a cavernoma, which is a type of vascular malformation.
The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and numbness, and had brisk reflexes and ankle clonus.
The patient was diagnosed with ischemic stroke, which is a type of cerebrovascular disease.
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla, which is part of the brainstem.

rationales.F01: Acute right-sided weakness and vomiting suggest a neurological event, increasing the likelihood of ischemic stroke.
rationales.F07: Motor strength deficits indicate a significant neurological deficit, strongly suggesting ischemic stroke and medullary infarction.
rationales.F10: The presence of a cavernoma increases the likelihood of a vascular malformation, which is a possible cause of the patient's symptoms.
rationales.F11: The recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla supports the diagnosis of ischemic stroke and medullary infarction.
